task_summary: Implement the 'Routing, Layout & Navigation' component (id: routing_and_layout) in TypeScript/React 18 using react-router-dom. This includes: ensureLeadingSlash utility, Sidebar and Layout components, createAppRouter factory, getNavLinkClassName helper, and associated types (RouteSlug, StepId, StepLabel enums; RouteEntry, RouteEntryList, RouteSlugMap structs). The component depends on 'page_content' module. Prior attempts failed because createAppRouter tried to dynamically require a non-existent './errors' module and failed to resolve page content modules at runtime.

findings.topic: React Router v6 createBrowserRouter / createMemoryRouter patterns
findings.finding: React Router v6.4+ provides createBrowserRouter() which accepts a RouteObject[] array. Each RouteObject has { path, element, children, index } properties. For testing, createMemoryRouter() is the correct choice as it doesn't require a DOM history API. The router is passed to <RouterProvider router={router} />. Child routes under a parent with path '/' should use RELATIVE paths (no leading slash). An index route uses { index: true, element } instead of { path: '', element }.
findings.source: react-router-dom v6 documentation and API reference
findings.relevance: Directly defines how createAppRouter should construct its route config. Tests expect: parent route path='/', 13 child routes, index route for home, relative paths without leading slash.

findings.topic: Root cause of prior failures: dynamic require of './errors' module
findings.finding: The previous implementation used a dynamic require() call to load page content modules and had a custom error class in a separate './errors' file. This caused MODULE_NOT_FOUND errors in two stages: first the './errors' module didn't exist, then after that was addressed, the dynamic require for route entry 'home' failed. The fix is to NOT use dynamic require/import at all. Instead, directly import the page_content dependency (STEPS array or similar) and use React.createElement or JSX to create route elements statically. The route config should be a pure data structure built from the STEPS/route entries without any dynamic module resolution.
findings.source: Analysis of error traces from prior attempts
findings.relevance: Critical — this is the exact mistake that must not be repeated. createAppRouter must NOT use require() or dynamic import() to resolve page components.

findings.topic: Slug handling — stripping leading slash for child routes
findings.finding: ROUTE_SLUG_MAP values already include a leading slash (e.g. '/step-0-cartographer'). When used as child route paths under parent path '/', the leading slash must be STRIPPED to make them relative. Tests explicitly verify: 'no child route path starts with /' and 'no double-slash when combined with parent /'. The ensureLeadingSlash() utility is for NavLink 'to' props (absolute navigation), NOT for route path definitions. For route paths: slug.startsWith('/') ? slug.slice(1) : slug.
findings.source: Operating procedures slug handling rules + test expectations
findings.relevance: Directly relevant — this is a common pitfall. Route child paths must be relative (no leading /), but NavLink targets need absolute paths (with leading /).

findings.topic: vi.mock() rules for the page_content dependency
findings.finding: Tests will mock the 'page_content' dependency. The mock MUST provide every named runtime export of that module with exact names (e.g., STEPS not STEP_CONTENT_LIST, ROUTE_SLUG_MAP not ROUTE_SLUGS). The implementation must import from page_content using the exact exported names. Based on the test expecting 13 child routes and the naming conventions, the page_content module likely exports: STEPS (array of 13 step entries including home), ROUTE_SLUG_MAP (record mapping step IDs to slugs), and possibly step component references or a ROUTE_ENTRY_LIST.
findings.relevance: Essential for tests to pass — mismatched import names will cause test failures.

findings.topic: NavLink className function pattern in React Router v6
findings.finding: React Router v6 NavLink accepts a className prop that can be a function: className={({ isActive }) => getNavLinkClassName(isActive)}. The getNavLinkClassName helper should return Tailwind CSS class strings — typically a base set of classes plus active-state classes (e.g., bold, colored text, background highlight). This is a pure function taking a boolean and returning a string.
findings.relevance: Defines how getNavLinkClassName integrates with NavLink in the Sidebar component.

findings.topic: Layout component pattern with React Router Outlet
findings.finding: The Layout component in React Router v6 uses <Outlet /> to render child route content. A typical pattern: Layout renders a flex container with <Sidebar /> on one side and <Outlet /> as the main content area. The Layout component is set as the 'element' of the parent route, and child routes render into the Outlet.
findings.source: React Router v6 nested routes documentation
findings.relevance: Defines the architectural pattern for the Layout component.

findings.topic: Type/enum patterns in TypeScript for route configuration
findings.finding: For RouteSlug, StepId, StepLabel enums — use 'as const' objects with derived union types or TypeScript string enums. Given the 'export type {}' rule, interfaces and type aliases must use 'export type'. However, enums are runtime values and use regular 'export'. For RouteEntry struct: { id: StepId, slug: RouteSlug, label: StepLabel, element: ReactNode }. RouteSlugMap should be Record<StepId, RouteSlug> or similar.
findings.source: TypeScript strict mode best practices, operating procedures
findings.relevance: Ensures correct export syntax and type safety per project standards.

findings.finding: The test expects exactly 13 child routes. This likely corresponds to: 1 home/index route + 12 step routes (step-0 through step-11), or 1 home + 12 steps. The home route must use { index: true } rather than { path: '' }. Each route needs a non-null element. The elements should be created from the STEPS data imported from page_content, likely by wrapping each step's content in a React component/element.
findings.source: Test expectations analysis: 'parent route has exactly 13 child routes', 'home child route uses index: true'
findings.relevance: Directly constrains the implementation of createAppRouter.

findings.topic: Named exports only — no default exports
findings.finding: All modules must use named exports exclusively. Components like Sidebar, Layout must be exported as 'export function Sidebar()' or 'export const Sidebar = ...', never 'export default'. The barrel file (index.ts) should re-export all public API members as named exports.
findings.relevance: Hard requirement that affects every file in the module.

recommended_approach:
**Architecture:**

1. **Types file (`types.ts`)**: Define RouteSlug, StepId, StepLabel as string enums (runtime values, regular export). Define RouteEntry as an interface, RouteEntryList as a type alias, RouteSlugMap as a type — use `export type {}` for these.

2. **`ensureLeadingSlash.ts`**: Pure utility function. Guard: `slug.startsWith('/') ? slug : '/' + slug`. Used for NavLink navigation targets, NOT for route path definitions.

3. **`getNavLinkClassName.ts`**: Pure function `(isActive: boolean) => string` returning Tailwind classes. Active state gets highlighted styling, inactive gets default.

4. **`Sidebar.tsx`**: Import STEPS/route entries from `page_content`. Render a `<nav>` with `<NavLink>` for each step, using `ensureLeadingSlash` on slugs for the `to` prop and `getNavLinkClassName` for styling.

5. **`Layout.tsx`**: Render a flex container with `<Sidebar />` and `<Outlet />` from react-router-dom. No default export.

6. **`createAppRouter.tsx`**: 
   - Import STEPS and ROUTE_SLUG_MAP from `page_content` (exact names!)
   - **DO NOT use dynamic require() or import()** — this was the fatal mistake in prior attempts
   - Build RouteObject[] statically: one parent route with `path: '/'`, `element: <Layout />`, and `children` array
   - Home entry gets `{ index: true, element: <HomeComponent /> }`
   - All other entries get `{ path: slugWithoutLeadingSlash, element: <StepComponent /> }`
   - Strip leading slash from ROUTE_SLUG_MAP values for child route paths
   - Return `createBrowserRouter(routes)` (or expose the route config for testability)
   - For testing, consider returning the route config object so tests can inspect it without needing a full browser environment, or use createMemoryRouter in tests

7. **`index.ts`**: Barrel file re-exporting all named exports.

**Key safeguards:**
- No dynamic module resolution whatsoever
- Strip leading slash for route paths: `slug.replace(/^\//, '')`
- Use index route for home (not path: '')
- All exports are named
- Type annotations on all public functions
alternatives_considered: Using dynamic import() or require() to lazily load page components — REJECTED: this caused all prior test failures due to module resolution issues in the test environment. Static imports are simpler and reliable.

Using React.lazy() for route code-splitting — REJECTED for now: adds complexity, and the prior failures suggest the test environment doesn't support dynamic resolution well. Can be added later as an optimization.

Defining route config as a plain array and having createAppRouter just wrap it with createBrowserRouter — CONSIDERED: this improves testability since tests can inspect the raw config. Recommend exposing both the config and the router factory.
Using 'as const' objects + union types instead of TypeScript enums — VIABLE: avoids enum pitfalls (tree-shaking, type-widening), but the spec says 'enum' so we should use TypeScript enums.

Having createAppRouter return the route config array instead of a router instance — REJECTED: tests expect a router instance (tested with RouterProvider), but we could export the config separately for inspection tests.
risks: CRITICAL: Prior attempts failed because createAppRouter used dynamic require() to load modules. The implementation MUST use static imports from page_content and construct JSX elements directly — no dynamic module resolution.
Mismatched export names from page_content (e.g., STEPS vs STEP_CONTENT_LIST) will cause runtime errors. Must verify exact export names from the page_content module.
Child route paths must NOT have leading slashes — ROUTE_SLUG_MAP values DO have leading slashes, so they must be stripped when building route config children.
The home/index route must use { index: true } not { path: '' } — tests explicitly verify this.
The test expects exactly 13 child routes — must ensure the mapping from STEPS to routes produces exactly 13 entries.
vi.mock() of page_content in tests must provide ALL named runtime exports with exact names — if our implementation imports something the mock doesn't provide, tests fail.
compliance_notes: All source files must be .ts or .tsx — no .js or .py files
TypeScript strict mode enabled — all public functions must have type annotations
Named exports only — no default exports anywhere
Use 'export type {}' for interfaces and type aliases, regular 'export' for enums and runtime values
Slug handling: ROUTE_SLUG_MAP values include leading slash; guard with startsWith('/') check; strip for child route paths
vi.mock() factories must provide every named runtime export of mocked module with exact names
All functions must have at least one test, tests must run without external services
Import from sibling modules using exact exported names — never guess
